events.text: Word goes round the isles that you sent a gift of the clouds to everyone you know. A crane lands on your sill with a note from an immortal you have never met: "I hear you are generous. I am also someone you know, now."

choices.text: Send the stranger a gift too

effects.log: A cup of cloud-tea goes back by the same crane. A month later the stranger sends a peach that tastes of a thousand years.

choices.text: Send the crane back empty

effects.log: The crane goes back with nothing. The stranger, you hear, laughed until the clouds shook.

events.text: By the reckoning of the Exchange you handed out spirit stones like a sect lord at a wedding. Two immortals now claim to have been neighbours of yours in the world below, and one of them even remembers the name of the street you were born on.

choices.text: Ask them what else they remember

effects.log: They remember very little else. You give them a stone each anyway, for the name.

choices.text: Send them off

effects.log: You send them off. The one who knew the name looks back once, and you are not sure, after all.

events.text: The pills you gave out are the talk of the Lotus Halls. A healer of the Jade Lotus calls, very polite, to ask where a newcomer to the isles found so many, and whether you would like to sell the rest.

choices.text: Tell the healer the truth

effects.log: You tell the truth. The healer writes it down, bows, and sends patients to your door for years.

choices.text: Say a gift is a gift

effects.log: "Of course," says the healer, who has not stopped looking at your bag.

events.text: A god of the neighbouring domain comes to your threshold holding the gift you sent, turning it over and over. "In ten thousand years no god has sent me anything," the god says. "What do you want for it?"

choices.text: Say nothing at all

effects.log: The god waits for the price that never comes, and leaves puzzled, and comes back the next year as a friend.

choices.text: Ask for a story of their domain

effects.log: The god tells you three. By the third you are both laughing, which gods seldom do.

events.text: Prayers of thanks rise to you from strange places: the people you shared your offerings with have shared them in turn, with their own worshippers. Somewhere below, a village you have never seen lights a lamp with your name on it.

choices.text: Answer the village with rain

effects.log: You send them a soft rain the next spring. The lamp burns on for a hundred years.

choices.text: Let it be theirs

effects.log: You leave the lamp alone. It is better, you think, for a gift to keep going without you.

events.text: Saengmo, Mother of Seeds, sends a gardener to your hall to ask how a god came by so many pills to give away, and whether you might share the recipe with her groves.

choices.text: Send her the recipe

effects.log: The gardener carries it home with both hands. The groves owe you a favour now, and they remember favours.

choices.text: Keep the recipe, send a pill

effects.log: The gardener takes the pill, and the hint. Saengmo sends back a seed that never quite stops growing.

events.text: On the cloud sea, where every immortal learns slowly, you notice it at last: what you learn stays learned. One evening on the edge of an isle the whole climb behind you settles in your bones at once, like silt in still water.

choices.text: Sit on the edge until dawn

effects.log: Nothing happens for hours, and it is the most useful night above the clouds you have known. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Test it on the old pine at the edge

effects.log: The pine bends and springs back, and your hands do not sting. Your body wakes.

events.text: A god forgets nothing, but you remember differently: every realm you ever stood in is still in your marrow, settled and quiet. In the stillness of your domain one night all of it lies down together, at last.

choices.text: Keep vigil over it

effects.log: You keep vigil the night through, and at dawn your domain feels it too. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Walk your domain end to end

effects.log: You walk it all, and every step is the one you meant to take. Your body wakes.

events.text: In your world, slow and kind as it is, you have noticed it for years: what you learn stays learned. Tonight by the ferry fire it all settles at once, everything you ever practised, like silt in a still pool.

choices.text: Sit with it until morning

effects.log: Nothing happens for hours, and it is the most useful night of your life. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Test it on the woodpile

effects.log: The log splits on the third blow and your hands do not sting. Your body wakes.

events.text: The body heaven gave you was a door below; above the clouds it is a window. One morning the sea of clouds parts by itself around your isle, and a column of light comes down that every immortal on the near isles turns to see.

choices.text: Walk into the light slowly

effects.log: It takes all day. By evening you know that heaven was never your teacher: it was your sparring partner. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Run into it with everything you have

effects.log: The light goes through you like a bell through a valley. Three isles see the pillar. Your body wakes, all at once.

events.text: Gods are made of heaven, and yet your body is more so. The light of your own domain gathers in you one evening until your worshippers below see a second sun, and fall on their faces.

choices.text: Let the light settle in you slowly

effects.log: You let it settle, ray by ray, until it is only you again. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Give the light back to your people

effects.log: You pour it into the worlds below as a long summer. The prayers that come back are new ones. Your body wakes.

events.text: The body you were born with in this world was always too much for it. One morning the clouds over your town part by themselves, and a column of light comes down on your yard. The neighbours come out in their night things.

choices.text: Walk into the light slowly

effects.log: It takes all day. By evening the neighbours have brought food, and you understand a great deal. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Run into it with everything you have

effects.log: The light goes through you like a bell. Half the river towns see the pillar. Your body wakes, all at once.

events.text: The cold you were born with has waited for the cold up here. On a winter night above the clouds it rises all at once: frost on the inside of your grotto, ice in the cloud-tea, and a stillness the old immortals stop to feel.

choices.text: Let the cold in, all of it

effects.log: For three days you cannot feel your hands. On the fourth your qi moves like a river under ice. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Let it out a thread at a time

effects.log: A thread at a time, for a whole winter of the isles. The cold learns your rhythm. Your body wakes, under your hand.

events.text: Under a god's sky the cold in you finds its own season. One night your domain turns white from end to end, and the prayers that rise from below are prayers about snow.

choices.text: Let the winter have the domain a while

effects.log: For a season your domain sleeps under snow, and wakes greener. Your body wakes with it.

choices.text: Hold the cold in your own breast

effects.log: You hold it all in yourself, a winter in one heart. It learns you. Your body wakes.

events.text: The cold you were born with has waited your whole life. Tonight it rises all at once: frost on the inside of your shutters, ice in your cup, and the dogs of the lane gone quiet.

choices.text: Let the cold in, all of it

effects.log: For three days you cannot feel your hands. On the fourth your qi moves like a river under ice. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Let it out a thread at a time

effects.log: A thread at a time, for a whole winter. The cold learns your rhythm. Your body wakes, under your hand.

events.text: The fire in your meridians always ran hot. Above the clouds, where there is no ground to hold heat, it stops running and starts roaring: the clouds around your isle boil off into steam, and the cranes stay away.

choices.text: Feed it your training, year on year

effects.log: You train on the cold edge of the isle for a season. When the fire settles, it settles as strength. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Burn it all at once over the cloud sea

effects.log: One night, one pillar of fire over the sea of clouds, and the near isles talk of nothing else. Your body wakes, roaring.

events.text: A god of the sun would envy the fire in you. One noon it roars up through your domain, and every hearth in the worlds below catches at once, all on its own.

choices.text: Bank it, as a hearth is banked

effects.log: You bank it slowly, coal by coal. What is left is strength that never goes out. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Let it blaze for one day

effects.log: One day of blazing, and the worlds below remember it as the Bright Noon. Your body wakes, roaring.

events.text: The fire in your meridians always ran hot. Tonight it roars: the water in the basin boils, paper curls when you read it, and the cat leaves the house and does not come back for a week.

choices.text: Feed it your training, year on year

effects.log: You train in the snow for a season, and the snow does not stay. When it settles, it settles as strength. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Burn it all at once on the hill

effects.log: One night, one pillar of fire on the hillside that the villages talk about for years. Your body wakes, roaring.

events.text: Above the clouds the body you were born with finally says what it wants, and the immortals of the near isles hear it say so. You dream of a red moon over the cloud sea and wake with your hands already in the dark forms.

choices.text: Give the body what it wants

effects.log: You stop fighting it. It is the strongest you have ever felt above the clouds, and the darkest. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Master it on the white stairs

effects.log: A month of nights on the white jade stairs fighting yourself, and you win. The demon body wakes, and it wakes as yours.

events.text: A god with a demon's body is a story the pantheons tell to frighten young gods. Tonight your domain darkens at noon, and the prayers that rise to you are afraid.

choices.text: Let them be afraid

effects.log: You let the dark have the noon. The prayers grow fewer and fiercer. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Turn the dark into shade for them

effects.log: You make of it a cool shade over a hot world. The prayers grow kinder. Your body wakes, and it wakes as yours.

events.text: The body you were born with finally says what it wants. You dream of red moons and wake with your hands already in the dark forms. Every cutthroat in the river towns seems to know your name this week.

choices.text: Give the body what it wants

effects.log: You stop fighting it. It is the strongest you have ever felt, and the darkest. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Master it: you decide

effects.log: A month of nights fighting yourself, and you win. The demon body wakes, and it wakes as yours.

events.text: The deep, still energy that gathered in you all your life fills at last above the clouds. You sit by the Frost Moon Pool one night and the pool goes perfectly flat, and stays flat, and the moon in it does not move.

choices.text: Sit until the moon sets, and listen

effects.log: You hear the water think. By dawn you are sure it heard you too. Your body wakes, as quietly as water.

choices.text: Play to the still water

effects.log: Every note goes into the pool and does not come back. An old immortal on the far side weeps and does not know why. Your body wakes.

events.text: The stillness in you fills under a god's sky. One night every river in your domain stops to listen, and the worlds below wake to find their wells brimming.

choices.text: Listen back

effects.log: You listen to your rivers until dawn. They have a great deal to say. Your body wakes, as quietly as water.

choices.text: Sing to them

effects.log: You sing, and the rivers carry it down to a hundred worlds. Your body wakes.

events.text: The deep, still energy that gathered in you so long finally fills. You sit by the mill pond one night and the pond goes perfectly flat, and stays flat, and the frogs stop.

choices.text: Sit until the moon sets, and listen

effects.log: You hear the water think. By dawn you are sure it heard you too. Your body wakes, as quietly as water.

choices.text: Play the flute to the still water

effects.log: Every note goes into the pond and does not come back. Fishers on the far bank weep and do not know why. Your body wakes.

events.text: One morning above the clouds every blade on the near isles hums at once. Immortals stop mid-step. A faction's armoury rattles in its racks. All of them lean, very slightly, toward your grotto.

choices.text: Draw your own blade and answer them

effects.log: One clean stroke over the sea of clouds, and the humming stops, as if they had been waiting for permission. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Go to the isle where old blades are buried

effects.log: You walk among the planted blades of dead immortals for a day and a night. Each tells you how it was broken. Your body wakes.

events.text: Every holy arm in every pantheon rings once, at noon, like a bell. The gods of war look up from their halls. All of their weapons are leaning toward your domain.

choices.text: Answer them with your own

effects.log: One stroke, and a hundred holy arms fall quiet together. The gods of war send envoys. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Go and listen to the oldest of them

effects.log: You sit a day beside a spear that was old before the pantheons. It tells you everything. Your body wakes.

events.text: One morning every blade in the town hums at once. Smiths drop their hammers. The market's knives rattle on their hooks. All of them lean, very slightly, toward your door.

choices.text: Draw your own blade and answer them

effects.log: One clean stroke in the empty street, and the humming stops, as if they had been waiting for permission. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Go to the old battlefield past the fords

effects.log: You walk among the rusted blades for a day and a night. Each tells you how it was broken. Your body wakes.

events.text: Above the clouds the cold in your body turns to jade. You sit under a pine on the edge of an isle in a snow squall, and the snow falls all round you and does not touch you once.

choices.text: Stay in the squall until it ends

effects.log: Three days. When it ends you are exactly as warm as when it began. Your body wakes, and the years slow again.

choices.text: Walk the squall to the top of the isle

effects.log: At the top the wind is a wall. You walk through it. Your body wakes like the first frost: everywhere at once.

events.text: The cold in you turns to jade under your own sky. Your domain's lakes take on the colour of your skin, and a god of winter comes to see who is making jade of water.

choices.text: Show the winter god how

effects.log: The winter god watches, and bows, and goes home thoughtful. Your body wakes, and the years slow again.

choices.text: Turn the god away

effects.log: You turn the winter god away at the edge of your domain, politely. Your body wakes like the first frost.

events.text: The cold in your body turns to jade. You sit under a pine in a snowstorm and the snow falls all round you and does not touch you once. An old woodcutter stops to stare.

choices.text: Stay in the storm until it ends

effects.log: Three days. When it ends you are exactly as warm as when it began. Your body wakes, and the years slow again.

choices.text: Walk the storm to the top of the hill

effects.log: At the top the wind is a wall. You walk through it. Your body wakes like the first frost: everywhere at once.

events.text: The Five Elements body fills slowly, and above the clouds slowest of all. But one season on the isles the phases turn once, all the way round, for the first time: wood, fire, earth, metal, water, and the cloud sea around them.

choices.text: Follow the cycle with your breath

effects.log: A season of breathing round the five phases. Nothing in you can be pushed out of balance now. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Turn it the other way: the cycle that overcomes

effects.log: Water quenches fire, fire melts metal, metal cuts wood. You learn the cycle of overcoming too. Your body wakes.

events.text: A god holds one domain, and you hold five phases. In your domain the seasons turn all five in one day: blossom, blaze, harvest, frost, flood, and your worshippers have no idea what to pray for.

choices.text: Let the five phases turn in you

effects.log: You let them turn until they turn in your breath alone. The worlds below have their seasons back. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Turn them against each other

effects.log: You set them against each other and learn which wins each time. Your body wakes, and it is hard to move.

events.text: It took longer for you than for anyone: the Five Elements body fills slowly. But one autumn the phases turn once, all the way round. Wood, fire, earth, metal, water, and back to wood.

choices.text: Follow the cycle with your breath

effects.log: A month of breathing round the five phases. Nothing in you can be pushed out of balance now. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Turn it the other way

effects.log: Water quenches fire, fire melts metal, metal cuts wood. You learn that cycle too. Your body wakes.

events.text: The body you exchanged for was never born in anyone, and the cloud sea does not know what to make of it. One night above the clouds it settles all the way in you, and you remember, for a breath, being nothing at all.

choices.text: Hold on to the memory

effects.log: It goes, as such memories go. What it leaves is a body that does not quite believe in limits. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Let it go, and keep the feeling

effects.log: You let it go. The feeling stays: that every gate of heaven is a door somebody painted on a wall. Your body wakes.

events.text: A god is a shape the world agreed on. The body in you never agreed to anything. One night it settles all the way, and for a breath your domain forgets what it is.

choices.text: Remind the domain

effects.log: You remind it, gently, what it was. It listens. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Let the domain be new

effects.log: You let it become something a little new. The prayers that come up are strange and hopeful. Your body wakes.

events.text: The body you exchanged for was never born in anyone, not even in a world you made. One night it settles all the way into you, and you remember, for a breath, the time before this world.

choices.text: Hold on to the memory

effects.log: It goes, as such memories go. What it leaves is a body that does not quite believe in limits. Your body wakes.

choices.text: Let it go, and keep the feeling

effects.log: You let it go. The feeling stays: that every gate is a door somebody painted on a wall. Your body wakes.

events.text: On a quiet isle an old immortal is practising alone: one art, then another, then for three breaths something that is neither and both. The immortal notices you at the edge of the pines and does not stop.

choices.text: Ask to be shown it again

ok.log: The immortal shows you, slowly, all the way through. "It was never mine," the immortal says. "It is just there, between the two."

fail.log: The immortal finishes, bows to the pines, and steps off the edge of the isle into the clouds.

choices.text: Watch from the pines until dusk

effects.log: You watch until you could do it in your sleep, nearly. Nearly is something.

events.text: In the Hall of Drifting Scrolls a slip of jade has fallen behind a shelf: two arts drawn as one figure, with a note in a hand ten thousand years old. "For whoever has the first half of each."

choices.text: Read it where it fell

effects.log: You read it on your knees behind the shelf. The two halves in you turn toward each other.

choices.text: Give it to the keeper of the hall

effects.log: The keeper thanks you and shelves it somewhere you will never find. Your hands remember a little of it.

events.text: Two immortals are arguing on the terrace of the Jade Court, loud enough to shake the cranes off the roof. One says the two arts must never be mixed. The other says the best technique of their first thousand years was nothing but the two at once.

choices.text: Ask them to settle it with a spar

ok.log: They spar on the terrace, grumbling. Neither wins, and in the middle of it you see exactly what the second one meant.

fail.log: They both turn on you, agree that the newly ascended know nothing, and go back to arguing.

choices.text: Leave them to it

effects.log: You leave them to it. Behind you, a crane is knocked clean off the roof.

events.text: A god of war sits on the edge of your domain cleaning a spear, and watches you train. "You do two things," the god says, "as if they were strangers. They are married. Shall I show you the wedding?"

choices.text: Say yes

effects.log: The god shows you. It is not a long ceremony, but it is a beautiful one.

choices.text: Say you will find it yourself

effects.log: The god laughs and goes. You find a little of it, by evening.

events.text: A prayer rises to you from a world below: a young fighter there has fused two arts by accident and is begging heaven to tell them what they did. You know what they did. You have the two halves too.

choices.text: Answer the prayer in a dream

effects.log: You show the fighter in a dream, and in the showing you learn it yourself.

choices.text: Let the fighter find it alone

effects.log: You leave them to find it. Some things must be found. You think about it for a year.

events.text: In the Archive of the Silent Hall the Lamp-Bearer holds its lamp over a page for you without being asked: two arts, one figure, written by a god who stopped being one long ago.

choices.text: Read it by the lamp

ok.log: The page gives itself up by the third reading. The two halves in you were always one.

fail.log: The lamp moves on before you have it. The Lamp-Bearer does not wait for anyone.

choices.text: Thank the Lamp-Bearer and go

effects.log: The Lamp-Bearer inclines its lamp. You go with half a figure in your head.

events.text: Past the Isles of Mist there is a pool the immortals call the Frost Moon. Its water holds the moon all day, and an old keeper there says a water root that sits in it long enough comes out something rarer.

choices.text: Go and see it

effects.log: You go and see it, and are told to come back when you are sure.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with

effects.log: You keep what you were born with. Not everyone needs to be rare.

events.text: You come back, sure. The cold is waiting where you left it.

choices.text: Sink into the Frost Moon Pool

ok.log: The cold goes past skin and bone and into the root itself. When you climb out your qi has turned white and still.

fail.log: It goes wrong the way these things go wrong: your root holds, and you are hurt for a season.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with after all

effects.log: You turn back at the last. The keeper shrugs: not everyone wants to be rare.

events.text: There is an isle where the tribulation clouds rest between storms, a bare rock that smells of lightning. A hermit of the clouds lives on it, and offers to show a wood root what lightning is for.

choices.text: Go and see it

effects.log: You go and see it, and are told to come back when you are sure.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with

effects.log: You keep what you were born with. Not everyone needs to be rare.

events.text: You come back, sure. The storm is already gathering.

choices.text: Hold the hermit's rod while a storm comes

ok.log: The bolt finds the rod and the rod finds you. When you wake on the rock your root is crackling like dry kindling.

fail.log: It goes wrong the way these things go wrong: your root holds, and you are hurt for a season.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with after all

effects.log: You turn back at the last. The keeper shrugs: not everyone wants to be rare.

events.text: At the edge of the sea of clouds, where the isles stop, there is a gap the wind goes through day and night. The immortals call it the Wind Gate, and say a wood root that listens there a winter goes light and quick.

choices.text: Go and see it

effects.log: You go and see it, and are told to come back when you are sure.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with

effects.log: You keep what you were born with. Not everyone needs to be rare.

events.text: You come back, sure. The wind has not stopped since you left.

choices.text: Spend the winter in the Wind Gate

ok.log: By spring the wind is not going through the gate any more. It is going through you, and your root has gone light and empty.

fail.log: It goes wrong the way these things go wrong: your root holds, and you are hurt for a season.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with after all

effects.log: You turn back at the last. The keeper shrugs: not everyone wants to be rare.

events.text: A god of winter keeps a lake in a domain of snow, and has never let another god bathe in it. The god sends word: a water root would be welcome, once, if you are not afraid of what it becomes.

choices.text: Go and see it

effects.log: You go and see it, and are told to come back when you are sure.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with

effects.log: You keep what you were born with. Not everyone needs to be rare.

events.text: You come back, sure. The cold is waiting where you left it.

choices.text: Bathe in the winter god's lake

ok.log: The lake takes your root and gives it back white. When you climb out, the snow on the shore does not melt where you stand.

fail.log: It goes wrong the way these things go wrong: your root holds, and you are hurt for a season.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with after all

effects.log: You turn back at the last. The keeper shrugs: not everyone wants to be rare.

events.text: The storm pantheon keeps an anvil where its gods forge thunder. Its keeper looks at your wood root and says it would make a fine handle for a bolt, if you can bear being struck.

choices.text: Go and see it

effects.log: You go and see it, and are told to come back when you are sure.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with

effects.log: You keep what you were born with. Not everyone needs to be rare.

events.text: You come back, sure. The storm is already gathering.

choices.text: Stand at the storm anvil

ok.log: They strike. You stand. When it is over your root hums like a struck bell, and the storm gods applaud.

fail.log: It goes wrong the way these things go wrong: your root holds, and you are hurt for a season.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with after all

effects.log: You turn back at the last. The keeper shrugs: not everyone wants to be rare.

events.text: In the domain of the four winds there is a hall with no walls. Its god says a wood root that sits there a season forgets it was ever rooted.

choices.text: Go and see it

effects.log: You go and see it, and are told to come back when you are sure.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with

effects.log: You keep what you were born with. Not everyone needs to be rare.

events.text: You come back, sure. The wind has not stopped since you left.

choices.text: Sit in the hall with no walls

ok.log: For a season the four winds blow through you in turn. When they stop, your root has forgotten the ground.

fail.log: It goes wrong the way these things go wrong: your root holds, and you are hurt for a season.

choices.text: Keep the root you were born with after all

effects.log: You turn back at the last. The keeper shrugs: not everyone wants to be rare.

events.text: In the Hall of Drifting Scrolls a jade slip is chained to its shelf. Its seal is a knot of words that slide when you look at them. "Three Earth Immortals tried that one," says the keeper. "Two of them still talk to the walls."

choices.text: Read the seal (Mind 100)

effects.log: The words stop sliding. They were never a lock, only a question, and you know the answer. The slip opens.

choices.text: Read the commentary around it (Mind 80)

effects.log: You cannot open the seal, but the margins are worth a century of any master.

choices.text: Leave it chained

effects.log: "Wise," says the keeper, and dusts it.

events.text: A faction of the isles keeps a mirage over its terrace: a garden that is not there, with a path that goes nowhere. Its elders test their disciples on it. One of them dares you to cross.

choices.text: Walk through it as if it were air (Mind 100)

effects.log: You walk through the garden as through fog. On the far side the elders are very quiet.

choices.text: Find the seam in it (Mind 80)

effects.log: You find where the mirage was sewn, and step through the seam. The elder who dared you looks pleased and annoyed.

choices.text: Decline the dare

effects.log: You decline. The elder shrugs: the garden will be there tomorrow, and not there.

events.text: A cloud skiff loaded with spirit stones has caught on a jutting rock below an isle, and its pilot is clinging to the rail over a fall that never ends. Three immortals are pulling at the rope and getting nowhere.

choices.text: Lift the skiff free alone (Body 100)

effects.log: You take the hull on your shoulders and stand. The skiff comes free, and so does the pilot.

choices.text: Pull with them (Body 80)

effects.log: Four of you, on three. It moves just enough.

choices.text: Run for a crane-rider

effects.log: By the time the crane-riders come, the pilot has climbed up alone, white as cloud.

events.text: On the Wind Gate's edge an immortal from the far isles is holding a line of novices against the gale, arms locked, and losing. One more gust and the line goes over.

choices.text: Take the end of the line (Body 100)

effects.log: You take the end and plant your feet. The gale breaks on you like water on a rock.

choices.text: Brace the middle (Body 80)

effects.log: You brace the middle until the gust passes. Your arms ache for a month.

choices.text: Shout for them to drop flat

effects.log: They drop flat. The gust goes over them. Not glorious, but nobody falls.

events.text: At a peach banquet of the Jade Court a quarrel between two factions has gone cold and dangerous: nobody is speaking, and everyone is holding a cup very carefully.

choices.text: Raise your cup and make them laugh (Charm 100)

effects.log: You say something you could not repeat, and both tables laugh at once. The quarrel is put off for a century.

choices.text: Pour for both tables (Charm 80)

effects.log: You pour for both tables, slowly. By the time you finish, they are speaking again.

choices.text: Keep your head down

effects.log: You keep your head down. Nothing breaks, tonight.

events.text: A disciple of a rival faction catches you on the white stairs. "My elders are wrong about you," the disciple says. "I would rather learn from someone they are afraid of."

choices.text: Take the disciple in, and face their elders (Charm 100)

effects.log: Their elders come to your door. You talk to them until they bow and go. The disciple stays.

choices.text: Send them back with your good word (Charm 80)

effects.log: You write their elders a letter of such courtesy that the disciple is promoted for bringing it.

choices.text: Send them back alone

effects.log: They go back down the stairs, and look back only once.

events.text: A cloud bank parts below your isle for the first time in ten thousand years, and under it is a second, smaller isle, with a grotto door that has never been opened.

choices.text: Knock (Luck 100)

effects.log: The door opens to a knock. Inside is an immortal's last breath of qi, kept for whoever knocked politely. It is yours.

choices.text: Search the isle first (Luck 80)

effects.log: Under a stone by the door is a purse of old qi, sealed in a gourd. You drink it.

choices.text: Leave it to the clouds

effects.log: By the next morning the clouds have closed over it again.

events.text: A crane lands on your shoulder at the Exchange, drops a jade token in your palm, and flies off before you can see where from. The Keeper of the Lotus Ledger looks at the token and sits down.

choices.text: Ask the Keeper what it is (Luck 100)

effects.log: It is the token of an immortal who vanished an age ago, and it names you heir to nothing but their name. The Court is impressed anyway.

choices.text: Keep it quietly (Luck 80)

effects.log: You keep it. Good things happen near it, small ones, for years.

choices.text: Give it to the Keeper

effects.log: The Keeper takes it with both hands and bows lower than you have ever seen.

events.text: In the Hall of Heaven's Register one page is written in a hand no god can read: it shifts as you look at it. The Registrar says the god who wrote it is still listed, but nobody knows where.

choices.text: Read the page (Mind 100)

effects.log: It stops shifting. It is a list of every promise heaven ever broke, and the god who kept it. You read it all.

choices.text: Read what the Registrar wrote beside it (Mind 80)

effects.log: The Registrar's notes are worth a thousand years on their own.

choices.text: Close the book

effects.log: "Kind of you," says the Registrar, and means it.

events.text: A god of dreams has wrapped your domain in an illusion for a joke: every worshipper below thinks you have gone silent. Their prayers grow frightened.

choices.text: Unmake the dream from inside (Mind 100)

effects.log: You find the dream's first thread and pull. It all comes apart, and the god of dreams sends an apology in verse.

choices.text: Speak through the dream (Mind 80)

effects.log: You find one sleeper who can still hear you, and speak through them. It is enough until morning.

choices.text: Wait for the joke to end

effects.log: It ends in a month. The prayers come back, a little reproachful.

events.text: A pillar of the pantheon's hall has cracked in a war of the gods, and the roof over a hundred lesser spirits is coming down. The god of the hall is away.

choices.text: Hold the roof alone (Body 100)

effects.log: You hold the roof of heaven on your shoulders for a day and a night, until the masons come.

choices.text: Hold it with the spirits (Body 80)

effects.log: You and a hundred small spirits hold it together. They sing to keep time.

choices.text: Lead the spirits out

effects.log: You lead them all out before it falls. The hall is rubble, and nobody is under it.

events.text: The Star River has burst its banks between two domains, and a ferry of souls is being carried toward the edge where the river falls into nothing.

choices.text: Wade in and stop the ferry (Body 100)

effects.log: You wade in to the waist and stop the ferry with one hand. The souls on it cheer.

choices.text: Drag it to the bank (Body 80)

effects.log: You drag it to the bank a step at a time. The ferryman kisses your hands.

choices.text: Call the river god

effects.log: The river god comes, eventually, cross at being woken. The ferry is saved, just.

events.text: Two gods of neighbouring domains have stopped speaking, and their worshippers below have started a war over it. Both gods are at the feast of the pantheons, at opposite ends of the table.

choices.text: Bring them to one table (Charm 100)

effects.log: You bring them together with a story about their own youth. By the end they are blaming you for everything, together.

choices.text: Carry messages between them (Charm 80)

effects.log: You carry their messages all night, softening each one. The war below ends in a truce.

choices.text: Stay out of it

effects.log: You stay out of it. The war below goes on a while longer.

events.text: A lesser spirit of a broken domain comes to your altar, trembling. Its god is gone; it has no one to serve. It asks whether you would have it.

choices.text: Take it in, and face the pantheon (Charm 100)

effects.log: The pantheon objects. You speak for the spirit until they stop objecting.

choices.text: Find it a better god (Charm 80)

effects.log: You find it a kind god with an empty hall. It sends you a prayer every year.

choices.text: Send it away gently

effects.log: It goes. You hear later it found a home in a quiet world.

events.text: A star falls into your domain in the night, and when you go to find it there is a small altar where it landed, older than the pantheons, with a bowl that has never held an offering.

choices.text: Put an offering in it (Luck 100)

effects.log: The bowl fills with light that is not yours, and gives it to you. Whatever god it was, it was generous.

choices.text: Read the altar first (Luck 80)

effects.log: Under the moss is a name and a breath of old divine qi. You take the breath, and leave the name.

choices.text: Leave the altar be

effects.log: You leave it. A week later the star rises again, on its own.

events.text: A god of fortune sits at the edge of your domain spinning, and one thread of the spinning comes loose and drifts to your feet: the thread of somebody's luck, somewhere below. The god pretends not to notice.

choices.text: Tie it back where it belongs (Luck 100)

effects.log: You find the place in the spinning on the first try. The god of fortune stops pretending, and laughs, and owes you one.

choices.text: Follow it down to its world (Luck 80)

effects.log: You follow it to a fisher who has had a very bad year, and tie it to the net. The year turns.

choices.text: Hand it back to the god

effects.log: You hand it back. The god of fortune likes you better for it, oddly.

events.text: In the back room of a ferry house an old clerk shows you a ledger written in a cipher. "The first kingdom's tax book," the clerk says. "Three scholars went soft in the head on it. You look like you could read it."

choices.text: Read the cipher (Mind 100)

effects.log: The letters stop dancing. It was never a lock, only a question, and you know the answer. The ledger opens.

choices.text: Read the clerk's notes (Mind 80)

effects.log: You cannot open the cipher, but the clerk's notes in the margins are worth a year of any teacher.

choices.text: Leave it to the clerk

effects.log: "Wise," says the clerk, and puts it back in the dark.

events.text: A trickster of the river towns has set a fog-trick on the market square: everyone sees a fortune in silver lying on the cobbles, and is running to pick it up.

choices.text: See through it (Mind 100)

effects.log: You see the trick plain, and shout it plain. The crowd stops. The trickster is gone by the time they turn.

choices.text: Find the trickster (Mind 80)

effects.log: You follow the edge of the fog to a doorway, and a very surprised trickster.

choices.text: Stay out of the square

effects.log: You stay out of the square. Someone loses their purse; it is not you.

events.text: A loaded salt cart has slid off the bridge at the ford and pinned a child against the rail. Four ferry hands are pulling at it and getting nowhere.

choices.text: Lift it alone (Body 100)

effects.log: You get your shoulder under the axle and stand up. The cart goes with you. The child walks away.

choices.text: Lift with the ferry hands (Body 80)

effects.log: Five of you, then, on three. It moves just enough.

choices.text: Run for a lever and rope

effects.log: By the time you come back with the rope, someone has found an ox. The child will limp, but will live.

events.text: The river is up past the second step of the town, and the old dyke above the kilns is going. Everyone is carrying sacks. The sacks are not enough.

choices.text: Hold the breach with your back (Body 100)

effects.log: You put your back to the breach and stay there until the sacks come. The town keeps its kilns.

choices.text: Carry two sacks for every one (Body 80)

effects.log: You carry until your legs give out. The dyke holds, by a hand.

choices.text: Get the old people out first

effects.log: You get the old people out. The kilns flood, but nobody drowns.

events.text: A crowd outside the tax house of the first kingdom is about to turn into something worse. The guards have their hands on their staves. Someone has picked up a stone.

choices.text: Stand on the well and talk them down (Charm 100)

effects.log: You talk until the stone is put down and the guards take their hands off their staves. The tax house lowers the rate, a little.

choices.text: Talk to the guard captain (Charm 80)

effects.log: You talk the captain into stepping back. The crowd, with nothing to push against, goes home.

choices.text: Get out of the way

effects.log: You get out of the way. It ends with a few bruises, and nothing worse.

events.text: A runaway apprentice of the Shadow Lodges hides in your woodshed and begs you not to give them up. "They said nobody leaves," the apprentice says. "You look like somebody who would help anyway."

choices.text: Hide them, and face the Lodges (Charm 100)

effects.log: The Lodges send someone. You talk to them at your gate until they leave. The apprentice stays, and learns a trade.

choices.text: Find them a ferry out (Charm 80)

effects.log: You find them a ferry down the river by night. A letter comes a year later, from very far away.

choices.text: Send them on their way

effects.log: They go. You never learn where.

events.text: A rockfall on the hill road has opened a cave mouth nobody remembers. Inside, on a ledge, is a lacquered box with no lock.

choices.text: Open it (Luck 100)

effects.log: Inside is a breathing method on a single sheet, written by someone who lived before the first kingdom. It is yours.

choices.text: Search the cave first (Luck 80)

effects.log: Under the ledge is a purse of very old silver. Sixty taels, and nobody to give it back to.

choices.text: Leave it for its owner

effects.log: You leave it. The next rockfall closes the cave again.

events.text: A coin rolls out of nowhere at the night market, circles your feet three times, and stops on its edge. The old stallholders gasp. It is a coin of the first kingdom, gone a thousand years.

choices.text: Pick it up (Luck 100)

effects.log: It is warm. The market decides you are lucky, which is almost as good as being lucky. You are both.

choices.text: Leave it standing (Luck 80)

effects.log: You leave it standing. By morning it is gone, and your luck is better for a year.

choices.text: Give it to a child

effects.log: You give it to a child, who runs off shrieking. You hear the child grew up rich.
